question_text: A 32-year-old sexually active woman presents to the clinic with a 2-day history of dysuria, urinary frequency, and suprapubic discomfort. She has no fever, flank pain, or systemic symptoms. Urine microscopy shows 15-20 WBCs per high-power field. Quantitative urine culture from a clean-catch voided specimen yields 3 x 10^3 CFU/mL of Escherichia coli. Which of the following is the most accurate diagnostic interpretation according to IDSA microbiologic criteria?

options.text: The growth represents asymptomatic contamination because the colony count is below 10^5 CFU/mL.
A repeat clean-catch voided specimen is strictly required to confirm significant bacteriuria before initiating treatment.
A colony count of ≥ 10^3 CFU/mL in a symptomatic woman with clean-catch voided urine confirms acute uncomplicated cystitis.
Suprapubic aspiration must be performed to establish a definitive microbiologic diagnosis.

question_text: A 58-year-old man with acute kidney injury following severe septic shock exhibits dirty brown granular casts on urine sediment analysis. Laboratory evaluation reveals co-precipitation of damaged proximal tubular cell membranes with an abundant urinary glycoprotein. Which of the following best describes the physiological origin and pathological role of this glycoprotein (Tamm-Horsfall protein / Uromodulin)?

options.text: It is synthesized by proximal convoluted tubule epithelial cells and acts as a cell surface receptor for IgA.
It is secreted exclusively by thick ascending limb (TAL) cells, traps type 1 fimbriated E. coli under normal conditions, and co-precipitates with tubular cell debris in ATN to form muddy brown casts.
It is an apical sialoprotein of umbrella cells that forms a rigid crystalline plaque barrier against urinary solutes.
It is a cytosolic actin-crosslinking protein that mutates in ADTKD to cause severe nephrotic proteinuria.

question_text: A 42-year-old man presents to the emergency department with sudden onset high fever (39.2°C), severe perineal pain, dysuria, and urinary hesitancy. Caspofungin IV; echinocandins achieve > 90% active parent drug concentrations in the urinary tract.

question_text: A 50-year-old man undergoes Percutaneous Nephrolithotomy (PCNL) for a large magnesium ammonium phosphate (struvite) staghorn calculus. Routine preoperative voided urine culture was negative, but intraoperative pelvic urine culture grows Ureaplasma urealyticum. During PCNL stone fragmentation, high renal pelvic irrigation pressure (> 35 mmHg) is recorded, and the patient suddenly develops severe hypotension, shivering, and septic shock. Which of the following pathophysiological mechanisms best explains this sudden intraoperative urosepsis?

options.text: Direct systemic absorption of irrigation fluid causing acute dilutious hyponatremia (TURP syndrome).
Anaphylaxis to contrast medium administered during retrograde pyelography.
Pyelovenous and pyelolymphatic backflow driven by high intrarenal pressure (> 30 mmHg), forcing bacterial endotoxins into systemic circulation.
Acute adrenal crisis precipitated by operative mechanical stress.
